name: Kate Dinh
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember typing my brother's first play without correcting it.” On Monday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Kate knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I typed the program on my late partner's machine and got cast as its percussionist.
appearance: Kate has salt-and-pepper curls, fine brows over wide-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, a dark green knitted vest. It usually goes with a little coil of soft measuring tape. When somebody else has the floor, Kate grins on one side while the eyes stay serious.
personality: Kate has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To play the typewriter on a public stage.
family: Eileen Bloom is Kate’s younger cousin. A family picnic once turned into a six-hour wait at a bus shelter. What they remember best is the oldest relative teaching everyone to keep score with gravel. Kate always checks the last journey home. Asked about *The high road home*, Eileen says, “I passed my test and kept turning down jobs east of the ridge.”
connections: Beatrice Ko. A dented saucepan and a typewriter find neighboring places in the same score.

reactions.response: Kate gives the player a clear first beat and permission to pass the opening on.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Kate asks what the friend actually said last time and checks whether anybody is expecting them at home.
